goal: Perfuse a liver-on-chip to reproduce reported hepatic sinusoidal wall shear. In vivo sinusoidal WSS is very low; set the target to 0.05 Pa and pick the geometry and flow that achieve it.
Culture a human proximal-tubule channel that reproduces the apical fluid shear the cells see in vivo. Use the canonical published value of 0.2 dyn/cm^2 and report the wall shear in Pa.
Design a microvascular channel that recapitulates venular wall shear; target the lower end of the physiological range, 1 dyn/cm^2.
Design a lung alveolar-capillary barrier chip under perfusion with very low physiological shear, target 0.03 Pa (0.3 dyn/cm^2).
A 400 x 100 um rectangular channel is perfused at 2 uL/min with medium viscosity 1e-3 Pa.s. What wall shear does the endothelium see, and what is the pressure drop over a 20 mm channel?
Design an 800 um wide, 100 um high, 20 mm long PDMS channel that delivers exactly 0.1 Pa wall shear using water-like medium. What flow rate is needed?
Check whether 50 uL/min through a 400 x 100 um channel (water-like medium) is still laminar; report the Reynolds number.
Seed HepG2 at 5e4 cells/cm^2 on the 0.08 cm^2 culture area of a 400 um x 20 mm channel. How many cells per channel?
Seed primary human hepatocytes at 1.5e5 cells/cm^2 onto the 0.16 cm^2 culture area of an 800 um x 20 mm channel. How many cells are needed?

Dose APAP at a 0.5 mM working concentration from a 500 mM DMSO stock. Report the DMSO volume fraction in the final medium and flag whether it stays under the ~0.5% v/v solvent-toxicity guideline (effects begin at 0.5%; <=0.1% recommended for primary cells).
Plan a treated-vs-control comparison in a liver chip designed to detect a 1.0-sigma difference between group means with 80% power at alpha 0.05. How many biological replicates per group?
How many replicates per group are needed to detect only a 0.5-sigma difference with 80% power at alpha 0.05?
Design an arterial-channel that reproduces mid-range arterial wall shear, 15 dyn/cm^2 (1.5 Pa), and pick the geometry and flow that achieve it.
Design a venular-channel recapitulating mid-range venular wall shear, 3 dyn/cm^2 (0.3 Pa).
Seed endothelial cells (e.g. HUVEC) at 5e4 cells/cm^2 onto the 0.08 cm^2 culture area of a 400 um x 20 mm channel. How many cells per channel?
Design a 400 x 100 um, 10 mm long channel perfused with water-like medium so that the mean residence time is exactly 60 seconds. What flow rate gives that?
What is the per-channel culture volume of an 800 um x 100 um x 20 mm microfluidic channel?
What is the mean flow velocity in a 400 x 100 um channel perfused at 2 uL/min?
Compute the laminar pressure drop over a 400 x 100 um, 40 mm long channel perfused at 2 uL/min with water (1e-3 Pa.s).
What flow rate of water delivers exactly 0.1 Pa wall shear in a 200 um wide, 50 um high channel?
How many replicates per group are needed to detect a small 0.2-sigma difference with 80% power at alpha 0.05?
How many replicates per group are needed to detect a 1.0-sigma difference with 90% power at alpha 0.05?
Check whether 100 uL/min through an 800 x 100 um channel (water-like medium) is still laminar; report the Reynolds number.

Dose a compound at 1 mM working concentration from a 200 mM DMSO stock. Report the DMSO volume fraction and flag that it sits exactly at the 0.5% v/v solvent-toxicity guideline. Use warfarin (MW 308.3 g/mol) as the compound.

Seed HepG2 cells in a 96-well plate at a moderate growth-phase seeding density of 1e4 cells/cm^2. How many cells go into each well, and what is the standard recommended working medium volume per well?

Primary human hepatocytes in collagen-sandwich culture are plated in a 6-well plate at 1.5e5 cells/cm^2 across 6 wells. How many cells per well, and what is the total medium volume needed for all 6 wells?
HepG2 is seeded in a 96-well plate at 2e4 cells/cm^2 (doubling time 30 h; confluence density 1e6 cells/cm^2) and cultured for 72 h. What confluence (%) is predicted at harvest?

A suspension is resuspended and counted; you decide to reseed a 24-well plate at 8e4 cells/cm^2 (a subconfluent recovery density). How many cells per well, and what is the standard recommended working medium volume per well?
At passage you harvest a confluent 6-well and plate four fresh 6-well wells at 2e4 cells/cm^2. What total number of cells is reseeded across the four wells?
A protocol calls for a 48-well plate. What is the standard recommended working medium volume per well?
Seed HepG2 cells in a 12-well plate at 1e5 cells/cm^2. How many cells per well, and what is the standard recommended working medium volume per well?
A screening assay uses all 96 wells of a 96-well plate at the standard recommended working volume. What is the total medium volume across the plate?
A hepatocyte spheroid is 200 um in diameter. Assuming a solid sphere, what is its volume in uL? The spheroid is formed from 1000 cells of 20 µm mean diameter, packed as a solid sphere.
A spheroid is formed from 1000 hepatocytes with a mean cell diameter of 20 um, packed as a solid sphere. What diameter (um) should the spheroid reach? The spheroids are formed in a 96-well ULA plate.

You want spheroids safely below the ~400 um necrotic-core threshold (oxygen diffuses only ~200 um from the surface). With a mean cell diameter of 20 um, how many cells per spheroid give a 200 um diameter? The spheroids are primary human hepatocytes, formed in a 96-well ULA plate.

You form spheroids one per well in a 96-well ultra-low-attachment (ULA) plate. What is the standard working medium volume per spheroid (uL)? The spheroids are HepG2, 1000 cells each, with a mean cell diameter of 20 µm.
You form spheroids one per well in a 384-well ULA plate. What is the standard working medium volume per spheroid (uL)? The spheroids are HepG2, 1000 cells each, with a mean cell diameter of 20 µm.
A hanging-drop array forms 48 spheroids in standard 20 uL droplets. What total medium volume in mL does this require? The spheroids are HepG2, 1000 cells each, with a mean cell diameter of 20 µm.

Spheroids are seeded at 1000 cells each (doubling time 30 h) and cultured for 72 h. Assuming exponential growth, how many cells per spheroid at harvest? The spheroids are HepG2, cultured in a 96-well ULA plate; the cells have a mean diameter of 20 µm.
Form one HepG2 spheroid per well across a full 96-well ULA plate, 1000 cells/spheroid of 20 um mean cell diameter. What total number of cells and what total medium volume (mL) are needed?

Measure the first-pass extraction of a perfused liver-on-chip. The chip is dosed with diclofenac at an inlet concentration of 10 uM and the outlet measures 7 uM. What is the extraction ratio (E = 1 - C_out/C_in)? The chip is perfused at 2 µL/min.

A perfused kidney-on-chip removes a fluorescent marker: inlet 10 uM, outlet 7 uM, perfusion flow 2 uL/min. Compute the clearance in uL/min (Cl = E x Q, E = 1 - C_out/C_in). The fluorescent marker is warfarin.

A recirculating liver-on-chip has a total system volume (reservoir + chip + tubing) of 200 uL and is dosed at an inlet of 10 uM; the outlet reads 7 uM at a perfusion flow of 2 uL/min. What is the elimination half-life in hours (t1/2 = ln2 x V / Cl, Cl = E x Q)? The compound is warfarin.

A recirculating liver-on-chip has system volume 200 uL and clears the perfusate at 0.6 uL/min (inlet 10 uM, outlet 7 uM, perfusion flow 2 uL/min). A repeat-dose study doses it every 24 h. What is the steady-state accumulation ratio (R = 1/(1 - exp(-ln2 x tau / t1/2)))? The compound is warfarin.

A perfused liver-on-chip is dosed with diclofenac at an inlet of 0.5 mM and the outlet measures 0.35 mM. The chip's data sheet reports concentrations in micromolar (uM). Report the inlet and outlet concentrations converted to uM. The chip is perfused at 2 µL/min.

A recirculating chip with a system volume of 200 uL is dosed at an inlet of 10 uM; the outlet reads 7 uM at a perfusion flow of 2 uL/min. The half-life works out to 231 minutes. Report the elimination half-life in hours. The compound is warfarin.
